Subject: Re: Order form question — legacy credits and invoice matching

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we review the revised order form (v4), the billing team at Acme has two items they need clarified before we can proceed with signature:

1) Legacy credit aggregation — our systems currently net credits across several legacy contracts and issue a single monthly credit memo. The redline in Exhibit B (section 3.2) appears to require per-invoice matching of credits to new Redwood invoices. Can we adopt an aggregation approach where legacy credits are applied on the monthly invoice roll-up rather than strictly per-invoice?

2) Invoice haircuts for partial-month usage — we saw a new clause that would prorate minimum commits pro rata to the day. Our accounting requires a short note about the rounding approach (round down to whole token-unit) and a mutual tolerance threshold under which adjustments are auto-waived.

I've attached a sample invoice extract (invoice_sample_202806.csv) that shows how Acme currently applies credits. Would Redwood be open to a short protocol that: (a) lets us aggregate legacy credits monthly, (b) provides a 1% tolerance band where netting differences under that threshold are waived, and (c) documents a rounding convention?

If you prefer, we can draft a short exhibit to the order form rather than rewording the main body. Need to get this finalized by end of month to hit our quarter-close.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

--
Monica Reyes
Head of Finance Operations

Subject: Re: Order form question — legacy credits and invoice matching

Hi Monica — great summary, thanks.

Short answer: we can likely accept an aggregation approach, but need to lock the operational protocol and tolerance language so Finance and Legal are comfortable. Laura / Ben — looping you in to propose redline language for Exhibit B. Key constraints from our side:

- We need an auditable trail showing how credits are applied (date ranges, originating contract IDs). Aggregation is fine provided the monthly roll-up contains the mapping.
- Tolerance band: 1% seems reasonable; we typically ask for an absolute floor (e.g., $50) under which differences are waived to avoid repeated micro-adjustments.
- Rounding: token billing rounds to nearest token; for rounding down we should be explicit whether applied before or after discounts.

Monica — we can draft an exhibit for your review that captures the three bullets you suggested and includes a sample reconciliation table. I'll ask Legal to produce a short redline and propose a DocuSign route for acceptance once we land language.

Can you confirm: (a) Acme is comfortable with a monthly roll-up that lists original credit IDs, and (b) whether the $50 absolute floor works for you along with the 1% tolerance?

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: RE: Order form question — legacy credits and invoice matching

Hi all — I drafted proposed exhibit language and marked up Exhibit B (attached: ACME_OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf). High level notes:

- Section B.3.2 (Legacy Credit Application): added a clause "Monthly Aggregation and Mapping" that allows Acme to aggregate legacy credits into a single monthly credit memo provided the memo includes a line-level mapping to originating contract IDs and dates.
- Section B.3.3 (Tolerance and Floor): added a tolerance band of 1% or $50 USD, whichever is greater, for netting differences. Differences below that threshold are deemed immaterial and waived by mutual agreement.
- Section B.3.4 (Rounding and Prorate Conventions): specified that rounding occurs after application of discounts and that per-day prorations will round to the nearest whole token unit; exceptions require written agreement.

Ben — I left a comment where Finance may want a short reconciliation table template (row: origin contract, original credit amt, applied to invoice ID, netting adjustment).

Monica — please review and flag any operational concerns. If you can greenlight the $50 floor we will circulate to Legal for final sign-off and prepare DocuSign.

Thanks,
Laura

Laura, Sean — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. The proposed exhibit looks sensible and aligns with our internal process. A couple of small asks from Acme Billing: 

- Can the reconciliation table include an optional comment column for "reason code" so we can note why any residuals remain (timing, disputed items, FX rounding)?
- For the tolerance threshold, Acme prefers the clause read as "1% or $50 USD, whichever is greater, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both parties" — i.e., keep the ability to raise the floor for certain enterprise accounts.

If those two tweaks are ok, we can accept the exhibit and I can route to our Legal team for final quick review. Please also include the sample invoice extract within the exhibit appendix so our billing team and yours have a shared reference.

Once accepted, we'll sign via DocuSign and start testing the monthly roll-up in parallel with our July invoice run.

Best,
Monica
